# [Baseline] - WIN - D - AVD Defender FSLogix Exclusions

Excludes on the AVD session hosts the FSLogix containers on the share, the temporary VHD(X) files, the FSLogix folders and drivers and the two FSLogix services from the Defender scan, as Microsoft prescribes for FSLogix.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | Microsoft Learn — Prerequisites for FSLogix, Configure Antivirus file and folder exclusions (consulted on 9 October 2026) |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_AVD_Defender_FSLogix_Exclusions.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_AVD_Defender_FSLogix_Exclusions.json) |

> The storage account is in the path as the CIPP variable %FSLogixStorageAccount%: set it per tenant in CIPP (Settings → Custom Variables) to the name of the storage account, before the first run. Whoever deploys with IntuneBackupAndRestore fills in the name by hand (in local/). The same variable as in [Baseline] - WIN - D - AVD FSLogix Profile Containers. Not included from Microsoft's list: the registry keys HKLM\SOFTWARE\FSLogix and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix (Defender has no registry exclusions; that line is for other security and DLP software) and the container mount points (no fixed path). C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Local\FSLogix is included as C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\FSLogix, because Defender does not know user variables. Defender resolves %TEMP% in the system context; the line is included anyway, as Microsoft lists it. As process exclusions Microsoft names only frxsvc.exe and frxccds.exe; frxccd.exe and frxrobocopy.exe fall under the folder exclusion of %ProgramFiles%\FSLogix\Apps. No other policy in the baseline sets excludedpaths or excludedprocesses, so there is no conflict. If exclusions for all devices are added later, a second Settings Catalog policy sets the same setting with a different list: that is a Conflict. [Baseline] - WIN - D - Defender Additional Configuration hides the exclusions from local administrators.
